A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 24-page FedGWC paper, including Appendices A–J. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish matching scientific content, with no material gaps limiting comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original classification and clustering experiments. Appendices G–J include sensitivity tests, additional comparisons, and analyses of clustering behavior.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 7 and Appendices G–J, including benchmark performance, sensitivity tests, and clustering analyses.

M1.justification: The Gaussian reward mechanism, interaction-matrix updates, affinity construction, and recursive spectral clustering are identical in Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR10, CIFAR100, FEMNIST, Google Landmarks, and iNaturalist coverage, including class-heterogeneity and clean/noisy/blurred visual-domain scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within every experiment. Table 1 retains IFCA, FeSEM, CFL, FedAvg, FedAvgM, and FedProx; Table 2 retains its separate comparator set, including FairAvg and excluding FeSEM.

E3.justification: Section 7 and Appendices E–I retain identical data partitions, client participation, model configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and hyperparameter-search settings.

E4.justification: The class/domain heterogeneity tests, RBF-parameter sensitivity analysis, baseline cluster-count tuning, and interaction-matrix and clustering visualizations are unchanged in Section 7.3 and Appendices G–J.

E5.justification: The result tables retain identical ± reporting. Neither version adds or revises repeated-run information, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match, including the appendices. For example, Table 2 reports FedGWC accuracy of 57.4±0.3 on Google Landmarks and 47.8±0.2 on iNaturalist in both versions.

T1.justification: Theorems 5.1–5.2, Proposition 5.3, the proofs and additional results in Appendix A, and the Wasserstein-score definitions and derivation in Appendix B are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusions retain the same claims about FedGWC, its theoretical guarantees, the Wasserstein Adjusted Score, and experimental performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of clustering and performance, privacy and overhead arguments in Appendices C–D, and the suggested application to malicious-client detection are unchanged. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added or revised.

D1.justification: Appendices D and F retain the same communication-cost descriptions, architectures, data-partitioning instructions, optimizer settings, and hyperparameters. Embedded link targets also match.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper and appendices, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to earlier federated-learning and clustering methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 5 February 2025 to v2 dated 1 May 2025. The manuscript wording, headings, terminology, and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–9, captions, numbering, and placement are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–24 are identical; page 1 differs only in the version/date stamp text, without a layout change.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendices A–J retain identical methods, evidence, reasoning, reproducibility information, and presentation. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and PDF metadata neither resolves a deficiency nor introduces a meaningful quality decline.
